analysis: descriptive phase/cadence audit; no significance or causal tests

function_schedule.interpretation: Function schedules were parsed only from active includes in each controlDict. Active probe-object count is derived from those includes, and each corresponding collected probe file is counted separately. Output archive absence is null/not collected, not zero rows. Per-step forceCoeffs, solverInfo, active probes and minMax data are supported by their configured cadence or observed per-step rows; global field writes are set to 100000 steps. calc_cp is configured writeTime but no matching artifact is present in the collected text archive; wallShearStress also uses writeTime and its present output file has zero numeric rows. Neither observation establishes whether its execute callback did work. The wall-clock function is first in the functions include order, excludes its first callback, and measures elapsed time between callbacks. Therefore a Time t sample is an interval measure, not an isolated same-Time output operation. No object-level cost is measured.

limits: The six runs are separate allocations, not repeated matched controls; no causal inference is made.
All six source loggers warn that 149 samples are below their run-specific 2%-at-95%-confidence recommendation.

Per-step function output is part of the measured interval, but no object-level timing, per-rank timing, filesystem telemetry, CPU frequency, scheduler elapsed history, or physical affinity telemetry is available.
IQR outlier labels and fixed phase bins are descriptive summaries, not a distribution-free stability or significance test.
The job history is unavailable; native evidence does not establish final scheduler state, exit status, elapsed time, or charge.
